# Menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component)

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="menstrual-tampons-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="menstrual-tampons-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="menstrual-tampons-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Menstrual tampons in the HMI library has 110 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, Ca and Sr from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel and chromium and others, in 110 results from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the menstrual tampons was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

## What counts as menstrual tampons

<a id="hmi-prd-001"></a>
<a id="what-finished-product-category-formulations-formats-and-intended-uses-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-002"></a>

<a id="hmi-prd-003"></a>
<a id="which-populations-and-exposure-routes-are-relevant-to-this-product"></a>

This page covers menstrual tampons, as sold (110 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Menstrual tampons overview

<a id="hmi-prd-004"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-product-category"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-005"></a>
<a id="which-purchasing-manufacturing-and-retail-decisions-can-the-evidence-inform"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-006"></a>
<a id="which-uncertainties-prevent-a-reliable-conclusion-about-the-category-or-a-particular-product"></a>

Menstrual tampons in the HMI library has 110 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, Ca and Sr from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Shearston et al. 2024 reported lead at 173 µg/kg (median), cadmium at 9.63 µg/kg (median) and total arsenic at 2.3 µg/kg (median) in menstrual tampons, as sold from all samples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the menstrual tampons came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

Labeled context, not menstrual tampons content results: 21 findings measured a related product, an ingredient, or metal released into a test liquid. <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-menstrual-tampons" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-menstrual-tampons-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component), group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:menstrual-tampons-289c46af2d1e:b25d4d143507"><summary>HMI menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component) Pb reference · Menstrual tampons, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:menstrual-tampons-289c46af2d1e:b25d4d143507"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component) Pb reference · Menstrual tampons, as sold. Menstrual tampons, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>173</td><td>173</td><td>173</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>173</td><td>173</td><td>173</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>1 reference units; 1 sampling family. <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component) FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-menstrual-tampons" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-menstrual-tampons" data-question="What heavy metals are found in menstrual tampons?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in menstrual tampons?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, Ca and Sr in menstrual tampons, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, Do V, Balac O, Nguyen K, Yan B, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Schilling K · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shearston2024-tampon-metalloids">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-menstrual-tampons-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-menstrual-tampons-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of menstrual tampons measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of menstrual tampons measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 5 groups of menstrual tampons ranged from 83 µg/kg (tampon TU2, made in USA) to 872 µg/kg (tampon TK1, made in Korea); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shin JH, Lee KK, Chung MH · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Sanitary Products of Women</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of the Korean Society of Clothing and Textiles</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shin2009-womens-sanitary-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
